title: Sepsis Vital-Sign Deterioration
scenario: A 72-year-old client admitted with a urinary tract infection is monitored over eight hours on a medical unit. The nurse reviews the flowsheet of serial vital signs.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Based on the trend in the flowsheet, which changes indicate the client is deteriorating and require immediate follow-up? Select all that apply.

options.text: Declining mental status from alert to confused

questions.rationale: Rising pulse and respiratory rate, falling blood pressure, and declining mental status together signal progression toward septic shock and demand rapid intervention. The SpO2 and temperature distractors do not match the actual trend.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Given the trend, which action should the nurse take first?

options.text: Notify the provider and initiate the sepsis protocol
Reassess vital signs in two hours
Document the findings and continue monitoring
Encourage the client to increase oral fluids

questions.rationale: The worsening trend of tachycardia, hypotension, tachypnea, and altered mentation reflects evolving septic shock; the priority is to escalate to the provider and start the sepsis protocol without delay.
